description:
A mutation reads the repository once instead of in three gated rounds, and the phase-to-phase coherence check goes with the phasing.

## Background

A changing mutation performs six capture rounds: two in a preflight session, three in the attempt session, and one at apply. The attempt rounds are an ad-hoc protocol in the command layer: a registry-only round, a round adding the event log and every indexed issue file, and a third re-reading all of it plus per-profile records, working-tree document paths, precheck prompts, and gate-run paths. An overlap-stability check gates each round against the one before it.

With publication comparing only the files it writes, the phasing has nothing left to certify. A mutation reads its base set in one pass, and a caller's named paths and listings join that same round. The apply-time round goes with the phasing: `JsonMutationSession::apply` still re-captures the whole read set and compares it entry by entry, and epic REQ-05 retires that revalidation. The preflight collapses to one round.

The base set does not take the event log whole. A whole-log read costs 0.89 ms/MB against a hardware floor of 0.81 ms/MB, and epic REQ-02 allows 0.34 ms/MB, so no implementation of a whole-log read fits a mutation's budget. The log reaches the base set as its length and a bounded tail — the value `EventLogTail` already carries — and the commands that parse the log name it whole in their own capture set. The label-update path holds no consumer that needs the whole bytes: its four sites are a composer prefix copy the positioned append deletes, a torn-tail inspection of the final line, a conflict preimage, and the apply-time re-capture this issue removes. The last two are conflict machinery that `ensure_write_set_unchanged` answers with length and tail.

The first cut keeps reading every indexed issue, because dependency-graph derivation and hierarchy validation need the full issue set to detect cycles and transitive redundancy. That cost scales with issue count, which is what the latency target requires.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A changing mutation performs one capture round in its attempt and one in its preflight, with no round gated by an overlap-stability check.
- [hard] REQ-02: No phase-one capture specification, phase-three specification, or overlap-stability check survives in the workspace.
- [hard] REQ-03: The capture's base specification reads the registries, the index, the event log's length and a bounded tail, the indexed issue files, and the plan documents a transition rule consults; a caller's named paths and listings are added to that one round. A command that parses the log names it whole in its own capture set.
- [hard] REQ-04: Gate-run result capture joins the same round, with its own further rounds gone.
- [hard] REQ-05: A pure producer reading a path the capture did not discover still fails typed.
- [hard] REQ-06: Capture remains budget-bounded, with no whole-worktree recursion.
- [hard] REQ-07: The change removes more lines than it adds.

## Notes

The phase-two closure-change retry test loses its referent and goes with the phasing; the property that a changed closure discards and recaptures survives as a single-pass recapture.

REQ-03's amended form was approved by the epic's owner on the measurement in `dev/active/7226f00b/whole-log-read-cost.md`, which also enumerates every consumer of the captured log bytes. Three consequences follow from it and are part of this issue rather than a later one:

- `CaptureSpec` needs a per-path read mode, so one path can be captured as length and tail while others are captured whole.
- A captured entry carries the length and the bounded tail. `EventLogTail` (`storage/repository_state_store.rs`) is that value, today private.
- `expected_of` stops deriving the event log's expected preimage from a whole-log SHA-256, because length and tail cannot produce one. Epic REQ-04 already names `ensure_write_set_unchanged` as the replacement; note that it has no production caller until publication is wired.

The five consumers that genuinely parse the whole log must keep asking for it explicitly, and none is on the label-update path: claim reflection (`repository_state/mutation.rs`), `archive.rs`, `commands/migrate.rs`, `validation/repository.rs`, and the in-memory backend's `load_events`.


## Decisions

- D-1: REQ-03's bounded tail is bounded by the final line, never by log history. When the tail window does not reach the start of an unterminated final line, the same capture round re-reads the log from its last newline, charged against the capture budget, so torn-tail certification judges the whole final line exactly as before. The mutation base never reads the log whole for this. Decided by the epic owner in session 7.
title: Single-pass mutation capture
